newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia Nov retail sales down 1.3, up 39.9 pct y/y.
newsitem.headline: Croatia Nov retail sales down 1.3, up 39.9 pct y/y.

text.p: Croatia's retail sales fell 1.3 percent in November from October but were still up 39.9 percent from a year ago, according to the latest official statistics.
January-November sales rose 21.6 percent compared to the year-ago period and some 400 leading retailers polled by the State Statistics Bureau forecast a rise of another 12.3 percent in December.

The November department store sales rose most, by 4.4 percent on a monthly level. They were followed by a 3.5 percent increase in vegetable and fruit sales, and 2.7 percent in clothing, leather, rubber and plastic ware.
The biggest slump of 23.3 percent was recorded in the sales of paints, varnishes and other chemicals.
Retailers' stocks, boosted by a 17.1 percent increase in meat products, 7.6 percent in oil and derivatives and 7.0 percent at department stores, rose 0.2 percent in November from a month earlier.
They shrank 1.3 percent from November 1995 and were also predicted to decline 1.7 percent due to holiday shopping in December.

Wholesale trade was down 4.7 percent on a monthly level, while rising 6.6 percent from a year ago but were seen as shrinking another 0.3 percent in December. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
